definition: Encore means an extra performance given because the audience demands it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word encore. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know encore should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Stamping feet and whistles brought the magician back out for an encore: one final trick with a borrowed pocket watch.
A finale is the program's own planned ending — impressive, but promised in advance, so it stops short of an encore.
A curtain call comes closer — the performers return to face the applause — but it stops short of an encore, where they perform again.

A reprise is the return of material the show has already presented once — the same music or scene coming around again later in the evening. An encore is defined by demand rather than material: it may repeat a favorite or be brand-new, but it exists only because the audience keeps clapping.

A bonus track is the extra song a band plans in advance and gives freely — generosity built into the album. An encore is never on the plan: it happens only because the crowd demands more once the program is over. Promised beforehand, the extra is a bonus, not an encore.
the first number of the night, played before anyone has asked for anything
the planned grand ending — an encore comes after even that

Encore is a whole French word wearing an en- costume: there is no 'core' inside it to peel off. Oddly, French audiences don't even shout it — they cry 'bis!', Latin for 'twice.' In France the word turns up in ordinary sentences, closer to English 'still' or 'yet' than to anything you would ever yell at a stage.
Encore means an extra performance given because the audience demands it.

Nineteenth-century opera crowds did not wait for the end: if an aria delighted them, they roared until the singer performed it again on the spot, and a single night's encores could stretch the show past midnight.
An encore is defined by who asks for it: the audience.
The scheduled numbers are done, the bows are finished, and the extra piece exists only because the clapping would not die down.
A planned bonus track is generosity; an encore is a demand honored.

Encore is the exact word for the audience-demanded extra at a live show, and by extension for any repeat of a triumph — 'a debut season that will be hard to give an encore.' Keep reprise for material repeated inside the program, curtain call for bows alone, and finale for the planned big ending.

The folk duo had planned a tidy seventy-minute set at the harbor festival, ending with the one song that had made them briefly famous a decade earlier.
They played it, bowed, and unplugged their instruments while the stage lights dimmed exactly on schedule.
But the crowd on the pier kept clapping in rhythm, and after three full minutes the promoter shrugged and waved the pair back out.
Their encore was nothing from the setlist: an unrehearsed sea shanty the fiddler had learned that afternoon from a retired deckhand.
Nobody had planned it, nobody had printed it, and for most of the audience it was the only song worth remembering.
